title: The Last Tryouts
premise: Wendell Vasquez has survived high school in Millbrook by being carefully, exhaustingly fine—until sorting her late grandmother's recipe box reveals index cards of directions that aren't for food: coded instructions pointing to records the school board buried decades ago. Following them, Wendell uncovers a pattern of expelled, erased students—kids like her—and realizes the board's beloved founder built his legacy on their disappearances. With the school's centennial gala days away and the board moving to seal the archives permanently, Wendell rallies the town's overlooked misfits into an unlikely crew. At the gala, they stage an unsealing that forces the truth into the open, costing Wendell her invisibility but giving her something better: a found family, a town forced to reckon, and the knowledge that justice sometimes has to be cooked up outside the law.
about_author: U. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former small-town substitute teacher who spent years collecting the stories students only told after class. They write from a kitchen table cluttered with recipe cards, some of which are actually recipes.

chapters.title: Fine
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A tour of Millbrook High through the eyes of its only out kid: the slurs she swallows, the allies she doesn't quite have, the performance of being fine. Establishes her survival strategy of invisibility and her grief-fogged numbness three months after Grandma Rosa's death. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Clearing Grandma Rosa's kitchen, Wendell finds the tin recipe box willed to her—but mixed among the cardamom bread and tamales are cards with no ingredients at all, just numbered directions and dates going back to 1971. The last card reads: 'For whoever's brave enough.' Emotional beat: curiosity cracking open grief.

chapters.title: Card Number One
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Decoding the first card leads her beneath the bleachers to a rusted maintenance hatch and a cache box containing a 1974 student ID belonging to Marisol Reyes—a girl Wendell has never heard of despite a mural of 'founder' Aldous Prine in the gym. Emotional beat: first thrill of discovery shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: Nobody Named Reyes
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Yearbooks from 1974 show Marisol's photo with her name inked out. The librarian, Ms. Okafor, goes pale when Wendell asks, then quietly slips her a key. First hint that adults know more than they say. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your town has a second story underneath.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell reluctantly recruits help: Theo, the stoner archivist kid; Priya, who runs the underground zine; and Dez, the janitor's grandson who knows every crawlspace in the building. Their lunch-table pact is awkward, funny, and the first real friendship Wendell has allowed herself. Emotional beat: found family begins as convenience.

chapters.title: What Prine Built
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Researching founder Aldous Prine, Priya maps his rise alongside a pattern: every few years, a student vanishes from the record—always queer, always troublemaking, always 'transferred.' The crew realizes the recipe cards trace these erasures. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Board Meeting, Public Comment
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell attends a school board meeting and asks one careful question about Marisol Reyes. Board chair Dale Hutchins smiles too long, and afterward warns her gently about 'stirring up hurt.' That night someone keys the word LIAR into her locker. Emotional beat: fear arriving, and refusing to leave.

chapters.title: Ms. Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor's POV (first departure). The librarian reveals she was a student here in 1989, when her best friend was quietly expelled and erased—and that Rosa Vasquez was the only adult who tried to stop it. Rosa started collecting evidence but ran out of time. Emotional beat: inheritance made explicit; Wendell holds a torch passed mid-run.

chapters.title: Sealed Until Centennial
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The crew learns the full archive was sealed in 1999 under a board resolution set to expire—or be destroyed—at the centennial gala, six days away. Hutchins is pushing a vote to shred it. The clock starts ticking in earnest. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by deadline.

chapters.title: Dez Knows the Walls
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez walks the crew through the building's hidden routes—the old tunnel to the records room, the alarm quirks, the gala setup schedule. Planning montage with heist energy, bickering, and growing trust. Wendell admits she's terrified; nobody laughs. Emotional beat: fear shared becomes courage pooled.

chapters.title: Rosa's Last Card
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Decoding the final recipe card, Wendell finds a letter from Grandma Rosa: she knew Wendell would be the one, apologizes for leaving the fight unfinished, and says staying invisible was never safety, only slow erasure. Wendell cries for the first time since the funeral. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Hutchins Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Hutchins corners Wendell with a deal: a college recommendation letter and a quiet apology if she hands over the cards. He invokes her mother's job at the district office. Wendell stalls, shaken—the threat isn't abstract anymore. Emotional beat: the cost of justice gets a price tag.

chapters.title: Mom
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finally tells her mother everything. Her mother's reaction isn't the feared explosion but exhausted fear—she knew whispers of this her whole life and chose silence to survive. A raw fight, then a fragile truce: Mom won't help, but won't stop her. Emotional beat: honesty fracturing and repairing family.

chapters.title: The Zine Drops
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew publishes a special zine: the pattern of erased students, redacted names, Rosa's timeline. It spreads through school overnight. Half the students don't care; a surprising half do—including alumni who start emailing scans of their own memories. Emotional beat: the story escaping its cage.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The board suspends Priya, searches lockers, and confiscates zines. Ms. Okafor is placed on leave. The crew's safe spaces shrink; Dez's grandfather nearly loses his job. Wendell offers to turn herself in to spare the others—and for the first time, they refuse to let her carry it alone. Emotional beat: solidarity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Tracking down Marisol Reyes herself—alive, seventy miles away, running a diner—Wendell hears her account: expelled in 1974 for loving another girl, name struck, life scattered. Marisol never got an apology and assumed no one remembered. She gives Wendell her testimony and her blessing. Emotional beat: the past is a person, not a file.

chapters.title: Sixty Hours
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Final planning under maximum pressure: the gala, the vote, the vault. Roles assigned, contingencies rehearsed, alibis built. A quiet scene where each character names what they're most afraid of losing. Wendell realizes she's no longer doing this alone or for herself alone. Emotional beat: calm before the storm, earned.

chapters.title: Centennial
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Gala night: bunting, speeches, Hutchins mid-oration about Prine's legacy. While Theo kills the lights and Dez opens the tunnel, Wendell takes the microphone during the toast. Her voice shakes; she speaks anyway, naming Marisol and every erased student aloud. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Unsealed
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The archive spills out—records, photos, testimony—projected onto the gym wall above Prine's mural as alumni in the crowd begin recognizing themselves and their classmates. Hutchins tries to restore order and fails spectacularly. The vote to destroy the records collapses. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as public event.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Suspensions reversed, Okafor reinstated, Hutchins resigns under pressure, and a restorative justice process begins rather than a simple scapegoating. Not everyone celebrates; some townsfolk double down. The crew reckons with what winning actually fixes and what it can't. Emotional beat: victory complicated, honest.

chapters.title: Marisol Comes Home
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At Wendell's insistence, the school hosts a ceremony restoring the erased students' names to the yearbooks. Marisol returns to sign hers, and embraces Wendell in front of everyone—invisibility fully abandoned. Wendell's mother stands in the crowd, applauding. Emotional beat: repair witnessed; inheritance honored.

chapters.title: The New Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. Wendell adds her own cards to Grandma Rosa's box—not directions to hidden things, but instructions for whoever comes next: how to find allies, how to survive a board meeting, how to be not fine and speak anyway. Final image: the misfit table, loud and full. Emotional beat: legacy continued, family chosen, hope practical.
